# D201 — Correct #486 implementation-review model attribution

The D188 decision and public issue text named actual Claude Opus xhigh for implementation review and independent QA. The dispatched implementation-review spec instead selected actual Claude Fable 5.2 xhigh. D199 and the prepared continuation accurately name Fable, but did not explain that change from the earlier role instruction. The catalogue audit found this documentation gap before any completed implementation-review verdict: original Fable attempt01 ended with quota429/exit1 and has no approval.

Under the owner's delegated model/blocker decisions, explicitly select Fable 5.2 xhigh for the #486 architecture and implementation adversarial review, and retain Opus 5.5 xhigh for the separate behavior QA. The difficult review is the evaluator-call provenance, side-effect boundaries, cause precedence, recovery and parent/child contract implemented under GPT Astra xhigh architecture. Fable is the owner's named architecture-capable Claude choice; it critiques the implementation independently from the GPT authors. Opus remains responsible for native/API/MCP/browser behavior QA. This selects the model by the work, keeps xhigh effort, preserves opposite-family review and separate contexts, and does not count planning critique as implementation review.

This amendment changes only D188's specific implementation-review model name. Its original wording, all actual provider records, failed attempt and frozen source633 remain untouched. Continue the same unfinished formal cycle1 after the reported quota reset using the prepared fresh envelope; no extra general scan or result is created. Preserve the fresh independent Astra MAX final audit and all numerical coverage, QA and merge gates. Current issue routing labels remain coarse historical routing; the written role amendment and provider records state the actual model.

Decline continuing to claim Opus performed a Fable review; decline replacing the required Claude family with GPT; and decline restarting the same unfinished review under a second model solely to conform to stale role prose. An Opus implementation reviewer would be technically viable, but Fable is selected for the architecture-heavy scope while Opus independently exercises behavior. No paid overages, early quota retries, source changes, plan-approved label or owner acceptance are implied. The catalogue preserves this late attribution correction and the eventual actual outcomes for consolidated owner review.

Parked follow-up from [PR #485](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/pull/485), [Claude Opus review FU1](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/pull/485#issuecomment-6898705327). This issue is outside the authorized four-intent batch and does not block #381/#414. No implementation is dispatched.

## Current behavior and impact

At source `615d50bc358d73bc55ad0591f4f625f1a46cb671` / reviewed head `656a73214c5d59a25c22a4abf2d8b3bf17976959`, Context Mutation and Exit have narrow authored-error classifications. Authored template or expression failures at the remaining evaluation boundaries still become `INTERNAL_ERROR` with their existing resumability. The new safe durable projection hides the evaluator cause from the inspector, REST and MCP; correlated server logs retain it. Authors must inspect server logs to diagnose these otherwise actionable authored failures.

Affected paths include script argument templates; heartbeat templates and predicates; subloop input/output mappings; inference prompt, context and file templates; and inference input/output transforms. A concrete native/composed QA witness is the authored subloop output-mapping `$error("qa-381-output-mapping")`: the new public failure is generic while its evaluator cause appears privately. [Public observation](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/blob/5082bc176e92cf3518abb630a5afc0a59c444815/docs/qa/2026-11-15-runtime-failure-candidate/internal/evidence-candidate-first/typed-subloop-mapping.json) · [Private diagnostic witness using synthetic data](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/blob/5082bc176e92cf3518abb630a5afc0a59c444815/docs/qa/2026-11-15-runtime-failure-candidate/internal/evidence-candidate-first/typed-subloop-mapping.private.json)

## Bounded outcome

Give recognized authored failures at these remaining call boundaries useful bounded public diagnostics and an accurate typed classification, without exposing internal messages, implementation paths or stacks. Establish provenance at the actual evaluator/template call; a provider or storage exception with the same class or name must remain unexpected. Specify resumability from the cause and preserve inference submission/acceptance evidence, script side-effect boundaries, cancellation/deadline precedence and parent/child parity.

## Acceptance and verification

- Enumerate each affected evaluation boundary and its public code, safe bounded diagnostic, node attribution and recovery policy.
- Positive and negative public-method tests cover genuine authored errors, successful evaluation and same-class external failures. Cover inference transforms separately from provider faults and final thread/serialization faults.
- Verify new stored events/rows, REST/MCP and the inspector against private server diagnostics with synthetic canaries. Preserve existing historical rows/events.
- Verify equivalent inline and nested failures, prompt/turn continuity, cancellation/deadline behavior and absence of repeated side effects.
- Update numbered docs, the guide and CHANGELOG; preserve all existing coverage and independent review/QA gates.

## Why separate

The #381 contract explicitly limits the new authored classifications to Context Mutation and Exit, preserves inference-transform classifications and avoids a general expression-error overhaul. Its documentation correction explains the remaining behavior. This follow-up addresses the broader authoring boundary deliberately.

Duplicate check on 2026-11-15 searched open and closed issues for authored errors, `INTERNAL_ERROR`, template diagnostics, `TemplateError` and `EXPRESSION_ERROR` with heartbeat. #381/#414 cover the current bounded change; #251 concerns inline/child parity; #98/#99 concern decision/Exit evaluation. No existing issue specifically tracks this remaining classification/diagnostic boundary. Preserve those scopes rather than reopening them.


## Intent 4 delivery admission — November 21

[D171 and its alternatives](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/427#issuecomment-7059806202) distinguish coordinator selection from human plan approval. Historical parking text above remains history.

Admission permits GPT architecture and independent Fable critique first. A separate written boundary/code/cause/provenance/recovery matrix and catalogued delegated selection are required before implementation. Preserve same-class external failures, cancellation, side effects, inference continuity and parent/child behavior; no broad catch based only on exception class.

Implementation and opposite-family review use the named routing models at xhigh. **Independent QA agent (planned):** `i4_486_behavior_qa`, a separate context and checkout; actual provider/session/build/evidence will be recorded when dispatched. GPT owns architecture; Claude Code contributes implementation, design critique, QA and adversarial review. Preserve touched-system positive/negative QA, unchanged coverage, current-head/current-target CI, fresh independent Astra MAX final audit and the three-general-scan cap. No implementation, QA or acceptance is implied by admission. Owner-only closure obligations and held460/Mac501 remain separate.

## #486 selected written plan and public evidence — D188

The coordinator selects immutable architecture revision 03 **with the A1/A2 amendments below**, after actual Claude Fable 5.2 xhigh returned **ACCEPT REVISED PLAN**. This is the owner's delegated blocker-decision route recorded in D188; it supersedes the generic manual plan hold for this bounded admission. It is not human `plan-approved`, owner QA sign-off, or completed engineering delivery. Owner review/rework of delegated decisions remains due before owner QA.

The five original documents retain their original bytes and historical “pending” wording. Relative filenames/source/probe links inside them refer to the retained local packet; the public comment mapping is:

| Original revision 03 member | Full public text |
| --- | --- |
| `README.md` | [Plan overview](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/486#issuecomment-7061823595) |
| `boundaries.md` | [All 26 boundary decisions](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/486#issuecomment-7061823961) |
| `expression-provenance.md` | [Evaluator provenance and alternatives](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/486#issuecomment-7061824217) |
| `verification.md` | [Verification and delivery handoff](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/486#issuecomment-7061824554) |
| `critique-disposition.md` | [R1–R6 / S1–S6 dispositions](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/486#issuecomment-7061825006) |

The packet binds source `02351e2fb932b3be44e7cc3fb3943a61d568226c`, tree `d289bb12b943557584c5659bc33447d1baebc2f6`, and architecture SHA256SUMS `1785227456c24297a90e68f96c18156e583f797d066c5363d5a8f3a3ce52728c`. Local source/probe/dependency inputs remain retained provenance; they are not all published as issue comments.

- [Actual Fable 03 report, verbatim](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/486#issuecomment-7061825341) — genuine successful provider terminal, exit 0, `claude-fable-5-2` / `xhigh`; SHA-256 `8a1c4fb12687d395daedfa59a099fe1779e93b6c675b2239cc0f6f035fc5243f`.
- [D188 selection and alternatives, verbatim](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/486#issuecomment-7061825658) — SHA-256 `5f67b74aeed4b0abaf3eb39aefe35e1c28611b1bd20133442ac49bacc1aacca6`.
- [Historical Fable 01 REVISE PLAN, verbatim](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/486#issuecomment-7061825963) — applies to revision 01 and remains history.
- [Attempt 02 quota history](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/486#issuecomment-7061826279) — provider exit 1 / `is_error=true`, no planning verdict. Its original quota message remains retained.

### Selected amendments over the unchanged revision 03 text

A1 selected verbatim clarification: Compile and unsafe-regex reasons attach only to the top-level compile(expression) of the invocation's own pinned source. The same checks reached through CHECKED_EVAL fail a run-time string inside the evaluator call and yield only the neutral evaluation-rejected fact. Add explicit tests for malformed and unsafe-regex $eval strings. Do not attribute their syntax to the successfully parsed authored field. Direct engine compile/unsafe-regex negative cases may bypass publish validation and must be labeled synthetic reachability.

A2 selected: At the newly typed JSONata sites the evaluator's own message is neither published nor logged, as at B20. Confirm removal of that old internal-fallback private record at those sites; update the affected docs05 diagnostic row and ADR0088. Fixed safe field/cause/action remains public. Existing harness/provider text, historical rows, P01/P02/B20/B25 and unrelated private diagnostics retain their contracts. Other new local diagnostics follow the selected bounded correlation policy. This is a scoped logging change, not a claim that all existing logs omit raw text.

### Implementation roles and retained gates

D188 escalates shared/core evaluator architecture plus inference/child integration to **`gpt-6.2-astra`, xhigh**. **`gpt-6.1-sol`, xhigh** handles bounded workspace, leaf-handler and public-child test tasks after the actual shared interface is frozen. The existing Sol issue label remains unchanged and describes bounded routing; it does not downgrade the selected Astra core role. Routing packet SHA256SUMS: `b00df574b3171926a0c953f8bab8fe53f63ea30f296207ccf4864b3f92972710`.

Exclusive file ownership, root-only index/commit/gates, actual Claude Opus xhigh opposite-family implementation review, independent touched-system QA, existing numerical coverage, current-head/current-target CI, the three-general-scan cap, reserved fresh Astra MAX final audit and signed merge remain required. Fable planning critique satisfies neither implementation review nor QA. Native filesystem, disk SQLite/restart, script counters, loopback HTTP and REST/MCP/browser evidence must stay distinct from scripted provider evidence. No implementation or acceptance result is claimed by this publication.

After all nine public comments were freshly read back byte-identically, admission removes **only** `needs-plan-approval`, retains `aidlc-ready` and every other label, and adds no `plan-approved` label.
